newsitem.title: USA: EDnet completes audit, states results.
newsitem.headline: EDnet completes audit, states results.

text.p: EDnet Inc Tuesday said its auditors Coopers & Lybrand completed its review of the company's results for the three fiscal years ending June 30, 1994, 1995 and 1996, and its financial results for fiscal year 1996 and first quarter fiscal year 1997 ended September 30, 1996.
For the fiscal year ended June 30, 1996, EDnet posted revenues of $2,536,258 compared to revenues of $1,253,336 in fiscal year 1995.

The company incurred a net loss of $1,154,403 or $0.36 a share based on a weighted average of 3,181,350 shares compared with a net loss of $394,323 or $0.35 a share based on a weighted average of 1,124,310 shares in the prior year.

Revenues for the first quarter ended Sept. 30, 1996, increased 39 percent to $926,000, compared to revenues of $664,000 in the same period last year. The company incurred a net loss of $566,000 or $0.12 a share based on 4,532,344 weighted average shares outstanding, compared with a net loss of $43,000 or $0.03 a share, based on 1,278,591 weighted average shares outstanding for the same quarter last year.

EDnet said it has adopted more conservative accounting principles in the areas of revenue recognition, expensing of research and development costs, and depreciation/amortization of tangible and intangible assets.
The company also announced that, subsequent to the end of the fiscal year, it obtained additional funding of $1,000,000 in the form of senior notes, and has other fund raising efforts in process.

The company added recurring losses from operations suffered by the company and its net working capital deficiency raise substantial doubts as to whether the company has the financial resources to continue as a going concern if current fund-raising efforts are unsuccessful.

The company said it expects continuing losses in the near-term, and consequently it recognizes it must continue to raise additional funds to fully develop our core business products if the company is to remain viable.
